Nup98 FG-region phosphorylation initiates nuclear-import failure and subsequent nuclear TDP-43 loss in TDP-43 proteinopathy models of ALS

Hypothesis. In human and rodent neuronal models of TDP-43 proteinopathy, corresponding to TDP-43-positive ALS, phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin Nup98 is proposed as an initiating, pore-intrinsic cause of selective nuclear-import failure. Loss of nuclear TDP-43, cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly, broader nucleoporin mislocalization, and neuronal death are treated as downstream responses. The claim is limited to this TDP-43 context.

Supported premises. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in cell models, and related pore pathology is present in ALS tissue; nuclear-pore and transport components associate with insoluble TDP-43 [S1]. These observations support a TDP-43-transport connection and leave the initiating chemical event open [S1]. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can arise independently of conventional stress granules, recruit or mislocalize transport-associated proteins, impair nuclear import, deplete nuclear TDP-43, and lead to cell death [S3]. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulates in those assemblies; that finding concerns TDP-43 and is separate from nucleoporin phosphorylation [S3]. Stress-granule assembly can sequester transport factors and impair transport, and altering stress-granule assembly changes transport and model phenotypes [S4]. C9orf72 repeat RNA alters RanGAP localization and nuclear import in a genotype-specific manner [S2]. No supplied source establishes nucleoporin phosphorylation as an ALS initiator.

Speculative bridges. Named kinases, sites, and phospho-dependent contacts are assumptions. Unverified prior knowledge holds that FG-nucleoporins, including Nup98, form the selective central-channel barrier and that proline-directed phosphorylation of FG-nucleoporins during mitosis disperses that barrier. The speculative chain places the same class of modification in stressed motor neurons: a proline-directed stress kinase, with CDK5 and p38 MAPK as candidates for empirical identification, phosphorylates Ser/Thr residues in the N-terminal FG region of Nup98. The phosphate is assumed to weaken FG-mediated selectivity and slow facilitated import of NLS cargo, including TDP-43. The initiating mechanism is Nup98 phosphorylation and the immediate change in pore selectivity. The downstream response is failed nuclear replenishment of TDP-43, cytoplasmic de-mixing, secondary incorporation of additional nucleoporins into insoluble material, and cell death. TDP-43 phosphorylation sits in that downstream assembly state [S3].

Alternative explanations. Sequestration of transport factors inside stress granules can impair import with an unmodified pore [S4]. Cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can inhibit import and mislocalize transport proteins, placing any later Nup98 phosphorylation downstream of TDP-43 pathology [S3][S1]. C9orf72 repeat RNA can impair import through RanGAP mislocalization [S2]. Broad cellular stress can also slow import, leaving Nup98 phosphorylation as a correlated stress mark.

Discriminating preclinical test. FG-region phosphosites on Nup98 are mapped by phosphoproteomics in iPSC-derived motor neurons that express an ALS-linked TDP-43 variant and in a paired inducible cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing system; sites are unknown until that map exists. Parallel time series then record phosphosite occupancy, NLS-reporter import rate, nuclear and cytoplasmic TDP-43, nucleoporin localization, and a stress-granule marker. The hypothesis predicts that Nup98 phosphorylation rises before import falls and before nuclear TDP-43 is lost. Replacement by phospho-null Nup98, with Ser/Thr changed to Ala at the mapped FG-region sites, is predicted to preserve import and nuclear TDP-43. Phospho-mimetic Nup98, with Ser/Thr changed to Asp, is predicted to slow import and lower nuclear TDP-43 in neurons that still lack stress granules and cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies. Combining the mimetic with suppression of stress-granule assembly tests sequestration: an import defect that remains favors intrinsic pore modification [S4]. Combining the null allele with forced cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies tests order: preserved import under those assemblies separates the proposed initiator from an assembly-only mechanism [S3]. A wild-type Nup98 replacement arm controls damage from nucleoporin replacement itself. C9orf72-repeat neurons are a boundary cohort [S2]; rescue in that genotype lies outside this claim.

Falsifying observation. In this TDP-43 model the hypothesis is falsified if Nup98 FG-region phosphorylation remains at baseline while import declines and nuclear TDP-43 falls, or if the phospho-null allele leaves the size and timing of those transport changes unchanged while the phospho-mimetic allele leaves import intact in stress-granule-negative cells that lack cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies. Phosphorylation detected only after import failure, and without an effect of either allele, is a downstream correlate.

Limitations. The choice of Nup98, the kinase, and the sites rests on unverified prior knowledge and on mitotic analogy, outside [S1]-[S4]. Phospho-mimetic side chains approximate phosphate only roughly. Acute stress in iPSC motor neurons omits aging and non-cell-autonomous contributions. A result in TDP-43 proteinopathy models leaves RanGAP-linked C9orf72 import failure [S2] and ALS without TDP-43 pathology unresolved [S1]. Insoluble TDP-43 can amplify pore injury after an earlier event, so co-aggregation alone cannot order cause and consequence [S1]. The design is a preclinical causal test and stops short of a validated treatment or clinical biomarker.
